message: openssl -days is over 200. Since 2026-03-15 a publicly trusted TLS certificate may not exceed 200 days (CA/Browser Forum ballot SC-081v3), and the cap falls to 100 days on 2027-03-15. A public CA will refuse or truncate this request.
fix: Use -days 90 and let ACME renew, or keep this key for an internal CA only.

message: openssl -days is between 101 and 200. That is inside the 200-day cap in force today but over the 100-day cap that starts 2027-03-15 (SC-081v3). This request stops working on that date.
fix: Move to a 90-day ACME renewal before 2027-03-15.

message: Terraform validity_period_hours is over 4800 hours (200 days), the public TLS maximum in force since 2026-03-15. On 2027-03-15 the ceiling becomes 2400 hours and on 2029-03-15 it becomes 1128 hours (47 days) - SC-081v3.
fix: Set validity_period_hours = 2160 (90 days) and drive renewal from ACME.

message: cert-manager duration is over 4800h (200 days). A publicly trusted issuer cannot honour it under SC-081v3; the certificate comes back shorter than the manifest claims, so renewBefore is computed against a lifetime that does not exist.
fix: duration: 2160h with renewBefore: 720h, and let the issuer own the schedule.

message: cert-manager duration is between 2401h and 4800h. Legal today, refused from 2027-03-15 when the public TLS maximum drops to 100 days (2400h) - SC-081v3.
fix: Set duration: 2160h now so the 2027 change is a no-op.

message: This expiry alert only fires with 21 days or less left. Under a 100-day certificate (2027-03-15) and a 47-day certificate (2029-03-15) the renewal window has already closed by then, so the page arrives after the outage is unavoidable.
fix: Alert at one third of the certificate lifetime - 33 days for a 100-day certificate, 15 for a 47-day one.

message: HTTP Public Key Pinning is being sent. Every major browser removed support for it, and a pin set outlives a certificate that is now re-keyed every 47 to 100 days, so it locks visitors out of the site it was meant to protect.
fix: Delete the header; use a CAA record plus Certificate Transparency monitoring instead.

message: TLS 1.0 or TLS 1.1 is still enabled. RFC 8996 deprecated both, current browsers refuse them, and PCI DSS forbids them for cardholder data.
fix: Leave only TLSv1.2 and TLSv1.3 on this directive.

message: Go tls.Config MinVersion is pinned to TLS 1.0 or 1.1, both deprecated by RFC 8996. Anything negotiating down to them is a downgrade path you are keeping open on purpose.
SHA-1 signing is requested. Public CAs stopped signing SHA-1 certificates in 2016 and browsers reject the chain outright, so this certificate cannot be used on a public endpoint.
An RSA key under 2048 bits is being generated. NIST SP 800-131A disallows it and no publicly trusted CA will sign it, so the request fails at issuance rather than at deployment.
fix: rsa:2048, or an EC P-256 key with -newkey ec -pkeyopt ec_paramgen_curve:P-256.

message: This text still states the old 397, 398 or 825-day maximum. The public TLS maximum has been 200 days since 2026-03-15, becomes 100 days on 2027-03-15 and 47 days on 2029-03-15 (SC-081v3), so anyone planning a renewal from this line plans it wrong.
fix: State the current cap and the two dated step-downs.
